primitives.name: Information Richness Ranking Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: A ranking system determines the information richness of each document within a search result.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_d': 'Information richness score of document d (dimensionless)', 'D': 'Set of documents in search result (finite set)'}
primitives.assumptions: Documents are scored independently on information content without explicit topic overlap consideration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R_d becomes constant across all d ∈ D, ranking loses discriminative power.

layer2.mapping: Maps document relevance to a scalar score via entropy-based information gain metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Average information gain per document in ranked list

primitives.name: Topic Grouping and Diversity Enforcement
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ranking system groups documents of a search result based on their relatedness, meaning that they are directed to similar topics.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G_i': 'Group i of semantically related documents (set)', 'T': 'Set of distinct topics (finite set)', 'D': 'Set of documents in search result (finite set)'}
primitives.assumptions: Topics are defined via semantic similarity thresholds; grouping assumes transitivity of document relatedness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When |T| < |G_i| for all i, or when G_i becomes empty, grouping fails.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to partitioning problem in graph theory where nodes represent documents and edges denote topic similarity.
layer2.telemetry: Number of unique topics covered in top-k ranked results

primitives.name: Diverse Document Selection Criterion
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ranking system ranks the documents to ensure that the highest ranking documents may include at least one document covering each topic, that is, one document from each of the groups.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_i': 'Selected document from group G_i (element of G_i)', 'R(S_i)': 'Ranking score of selected document S_i (scalar)', 'D_{top}': 'Top-ranked subset of documents (subset of D)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each group contributes exactly one representative to final ranking; selection prioritizes high-R(S_i) within each group.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If any G_i is empty, selection cannot be completed; if |D_{top}| < |T|, diversity constraint violated.

layer2.mapping: Applies maximum marginal relevance (MMR) principle to select diverse yet informative documents.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of selected documents representing distinct topics in top-k results

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism operates through a two-stage process: first, documents are evaluated for information richness using entropy or KL-divergence-based measures, assigning scalar scores R_d. Second, documents are clustered into topic groups G_i based on semantic similarity or co-occurrence statistics. The final ranking enforces diversity by selecting the highest-scoring document from each group, ensuring coverage of all topics. This dual optimization balances informativeness and variety, preventing dominance by a single topic. Failure modes include degenerate cases where all documents have equal R_d or where clustering fails due to insufficient topic separation. The system's robustness depends on accurate estimation of document relevance and topic boundaries.
